item.title: Abu Dhabi’s ADIC Hires BlackRock Veteran to Lead Real Assets
item.description: The Abu Dhabi Investment Council has hired a former BlackRock Inc. and Macquarie Group executive to lead its real assets business, underscoring the emirate’s ability to attract senior global investment talent despite regional geopolitical tensions.

item.title: Z.AI Set to Be First China AI Firm With $1 Billion Annual Sales
item.description: Z.AI is on track for annual recurring revenue of $1 billion, a significant ramp-up for an enterprise-focused AI startup trying to fend off a host of rivals in an intensely competitive Chinese field.

item.title: Michael Burry Says ‘Good Time’ to Chase Hong Kong Stock Bargains
item.description: Michael Burry, the investor made famous in The Big Short, recommends bargain hunting in Hong Kong’s stock market after it lagged peers during the global AI rally this year.

item.title: Coronation Trims TSMC, SK Hynix on AI Hype, Boosts India Stocks
item.description: Coronation Asset Management Ltd., which oversees $47 billion, has trimmed its exposure to chipmakers and increased its allocation to India, as expectations for artificial intelligence stocks have risen to levels that are nearly impossible to beat.

item.title: NSE Stock Draws Rare ‘Sell’ Call Ahead of Long-Awaited IPO Debut
item.description: National Stock Exchange of India Ltd., the operator of the world’s largest derivatives exchange by trading volume, has received a ‘sell’ recommendation just as it gears up to launch the country’s biggest initial public offering.

item.title: Wheat Eases as Traders Lock In Gains, Assess Black Sea Threats
item.description: Wheat extended a decline as traders took profits, against a backdrop of Black Sea supply risks and weak US export demand.

item.title: RBI Governor Flags Elevated Inflation, Monsoon as Key Risks
item.description: India’s inflation remains elevated, with ongoing tensions in the Middle East and prospects of a weak monsoon season seen as key risks for the economy, according to Reserve Bank Governor Sanjay Malhotra.

item.title: Howden Plots Giant Capital Raise on Path to Blockbuster IPO
item.description: Howden Group, the London-based insurance broker that’s chasing an initial public offering by 2030, is in talks to raise several billion pounds in new private capital as it seeks to maintain its break-neck expansion.

item.title: Japan LDP Seeks to Rein in ‘Excessive’ Activist Proposals
item.description: A Japanese ruling party panel is calling for stricter limits on shareholder rights, arguing that existing regulations encourage what it sees as “excessive” activist proposals and the pursuit of short-term profits.

item.title: Eoptolink Is Said to File for Up to $5 Billion Hong Kong Listing
item.description: Eoptolink Technology Inc., a Chinese maker of optical transceivers, has filed confidentially for a multibillion-dollar listing in Hong Kong, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: ECB Set to Wait for September to Hike One Last Time, Poll Shows
item.description: The European Central Bank will probably pause to assess inflation next week before delivering a final interest-rate hike in September, economists say.

item.title: Malaysian Growth Surges to 5.8% as Services, Tech Sales Counter Impact of War
item.description: Malaysia reported a surprise surge in economic growth in the second quarter as robust services and electronics exports countered the impact of the war in the Middle East.

item.title: EM Stocks Headed For Weekly Loss on Tech Selloff, Rising Crude
item.description: Emerging-market equities fell for a second day and are headed for a weekly decline as concerns over stretched AI valuations dragged technology shares lower, triggering a selloff across Asia.

item.title: Chip Stock Rout Deepens as TSMC Selloff Drives Taiwan Correction
item.description: Taiwan stocks fell into a technical correction, amid broad losses in Asia’s chip sector as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.’s results stoked worries over heavy spending and a weaker outlook for profitability.

item.title: Hong Kong Stocks’ Discount to China Widens on Liquidity Pressure
item.description: Hong Kong stocks’ valuation discount to their mainland-listed counterparts is widening, driven largely by liquidity strains and Beijing’s crackdowns on capital outflows.

item.title: India Chemical Shares Surge on Hormuz Disruption, Better Pricing
item.description: For the broader rally to sustain, demand will need to recover too.

item.title: Xi Vows to Make AI for All in Debut at China’s Top Tech Summit
item.description: President Xi Jinping hailed China’s progress in developing low-cost artificial intelligence, pressing his personal imprint on the country’s rapidly expanding global influence to call for a more open technological order.

item.title: Industrial Metals Decline as Traders Weigh Fed Rate Outlook
item.description: Base metals retreated on Friday as traders weighed the likelihood of higher interest rates and their negative impact on demand.

item.title: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank Eye FX Deposits For Margin Boost
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India’s latest measures to attract foreign currency inflows are set to lift optimism when some of the country’s largest private sector banks report on Saturday.

item.title: Mitsubishi Electric Eyes Power-Chip Merger With Rohm and Toshiba
item.description: Mitsubishi Electric Corp. seeks to reach a deal by September with rivals Toshiba Corp. and Rohm Co. to combine their power semiconductor operations.

item.title: China Chip Stock Pullback Drives Investor Fear to Four-Year High
item.description: A measure of investor sentiment on China technology hardware is flashing its most bearish reading in over four years as the red-hot rally in chip stocks rapidly cools.

item.title: Tata Group Resorts to Older Tech to Launch Its Chip Foray
item.description: Tata Electronics Pvt. is preparing to make India’s first semiconductor wafers on far older technology than it originally expected, underscoring the challenges the country faces in trying to build a domestic chip industry from scratch.

item.title: Modi Adviser Urges India to Seek More Chinese Investment, Trade
item.description: India should deepen economic ties with Beijing by opening the door to greater Chinese investment and reconsidering regional trade pacts as shifting geopolitics make the US a less dependable partner, an adviser to Prime Minister Narendra Modi said.

item.title: Investor Srinivasan Seeks Meeting with Anwar’s Office After Raid
item.description: Investor Balaji Srinivasan requested a meeting with the office of Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, days after immigration officers raided his startup school in Forest City, a mega-development in the southern state of Johor.

item.title: Japan’s ‘Decisive Action’ Threat Does Little to Scare Yen Bears
item.description: Japan’s Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama used her strongest language in weeks to warn of possible intervention in the currency market, but did little to scare yen speculators as the currency continues to hover near its lowest level in four decades.

item.title: Japan’s Stocks Dive as Investors Worry About AI Rally’s Run
item.description: Japanese stocks tumbled as a sharp selloff on Wall Street sparked renewed concerns over the sustainability of the global artificial intelligence rally.

item.title: Taco Bell Pulls Lettuce in Some States After Cyclospora Outbreak
item.description: Taco Bell said it has voluntarily removed potentially affected lettuce from a supplier linked to a multistate Cyclospora outbreak and will replace the ingredient within 24 hours at restaurants in affected states.

item.title: DeepSeek Champions China’s Bid to Flood the World With Cheap AI
item.description: On a video conference call from Hangzhou earlier this year, one of China’s hottest startups held a four-hour pitch meeting with potential venture investors that was unusual by almost any measure. Only two representatives per institution were allowed. The majority of those present were getting a glimpse of the company’s leader for the very first time.
